messages.content: (High-priority edits): Rewrite the abstract in plain language, not LLM outputs.
Also, re: story, see my comments on the bold paragraph titles of Section 2. I think if you string the necessary sentences from there together, you'll have a good draft of a lot of the abstract
"Guarded" is an odd term. We should use the term Armijo uses, because that is a technical term that will be recognized / is searchable. Alternatively, can use 'safe' here.
This is probably imprecise. For numerical reasons, it is almost always required that R \succ 0

(High-priority edits): This is an example of technical definition that is not clear intuitively. What is the idea of doing this? (To target the collection of new data to cases where the policy has some ability, but does not have mastery)
Again, too technical and lacking insight for the reader. The idea (as I understand it) is that we will trade off some stability margin on easier cases in order to provably stabilize harder cases

The idea here needs to be clear. Likely only requires maybe 2-3 sentences before the math to situate what's going on. 

E.g., most of the first block of text can be "we follow the method of Boffi, et. al., which ultimately bounds sample error via bounding successive differences [your nice visual equation]"

This should be posed as the foundation of what we are doing: following the ideas of Boffi!
This is the beginning of novel continuation -- building this into a feedback loop using the domain randomization ideas of Fujinami, et. al., etc

This is the big novel component -- By iterating on Boffi for certificate learning and Fujinami for domain-randomized control, we seek to iteratively generate controllers and certificates while only requiring finite-horizon cost realizations!
Again, see previous comment re: replacing "guarded"
This is a great opportunity to clarify the procedure! How does a single iteration work?
Important tip: every mathematical proof is obvious in hindsight. There is no need to devalue it by calling it 'elementary' (even if you think it is so)!
The meaning of these results is not clear to me, and they need to be discussed in more detail if they are going to be included. What is this plot showing, and how does it tie into the story?

This is actually a very interesting result! The robustness is clearly increasing! 

Is there a way we can falsify this? Can we run PPO with uniform data allocation and see how the policy robustness evolves over training iterations?

It's a little odd to me that this draft does not include the references included in the proposal. When you add the Appendix with proofs, etc, I recommend including the original proposal in the Appendix as well. If you have time, I would work in some of that introductory material and motivation into the doc, if you have space

Can boundary-targeted training enlarge a controller's acceptable operating
conditions? We connect trajectory-based certificate learning to a guarded
linear-controller update, with an elementary generalization proof, a
stability-preserving update, and a numerical study of how its components interact.
The chosen certificate sets how far each update can go, while the training target
matters only when plants disagree. Our main goal is now to prove when an update
enlarges coverage.
